# Better Scholar 2.39.2 — guide for AI agents

Better Scholar is a Chrome extension for Google Scholar profile pages (scholar.google.*/citations). It colours the rows where the profile's owner is first, co-first, second or last author, adds venue rank chips (CCF 2026 and CORE/ICORE 2026 lists), award and talk chips (Oral, Spotlight, Highlight, best paper), and a panel with a role × rank table, filters, citation totals and copy / export buttons. Everything runs in the browser. What it asks of the network: Scholar's own pages (the "Show more" button when `autoLoad` is on, and a paper's page when the user presses the button that reads full author lists), and paper titles to Semantic Scholar when `semanticScholar` is on. Nothing else is sent.

Two things you can do:
1. **Set it up for the user** — decide the settings from what they ask for ("Settings" below) and give them one JSON object to paste.
2. **Read or drive it on an open profile page** — page events ("Page events" below); no setup needed.

## Set it up for the user

1. Read what the user wants. Use only the settings listed below; do not invent any.
2. Reply with **one JSON object** that holds only the settings to change, in the shape of the record under "Current settings" (nested objects, as in the examples; no dotted paths). Leave out what stays as it is.
3. The user pastes it into *Settings → Configuration → Config editor* and presses **Apply** (or saves it as a `.json` file and uses *Import file*). The page then says what it applied and what it ignored. If something was ignored, ask the user to send you that message and correct the object.

Example — years chart off, BibTeX and summary buttons first, last-author rows only, bar-style rows:
```json
{"panel":{"years":{"show":false},"copy":{"order":["bibtex","summary"]}},"roles":{"first":false,"cofirst":false,"second":false,"last":true},"rows":{"style":"bar"}}
```

Rules:
- `semanticScholar` sends paper titles to a third party: turn it on only if the user asks for it. No preset touches it.
- The table of settings is in the order of the screen, top to bottom. `panel.show: false` hides the whole panel; every other `panel.*` setting then has no effect. A part's `show` switch hides the part, the switches inside it hide single things; the `order` lists only move things and never hide (a part left out of a list follows the others in the default order).
- The copy buttons, the table and the awards counts are also in the toolbar popup, under the same switches.
- What you see is what you search and copy: a rank list (CCF, CORE) or a kind of mark (award, oral, spotlight, highlight) that nothing draws — no chip (`rows.*`), no table tab (`panel.table.ccf`, `panel.table.core`), no count row (`panel.marks.*`) — is also left out of the search and of the exports.
- Colours are `"#rrggbb"` only; `""` restores the built-in colour of a role.
- A language is a code from the list below. Changing `language` reloads the settings page.
- Not settings, so not in the JSON: the Semantic Scholar API key, the spellings of the user's name (kept per profile) and the cache of paper details; the user sets those on the settings page itself.

### Presets
Ready-made patches (the settings page has a button for each); a preset changes only the settings it names:
- `all`: `{"roles":{"first":true,"cofirst":true,"second":true,"last":true},"rows":{"name":true,"style":"full","ccf":true,"core":true,"award":true,"oral":true,"spotlight":true,"highlight":true},"panel":{"show":true,"header":{"name":true,"settings":true,"fold":true},"filters":{"bar":true,"show":true,"search":true,"only":true,"years":true},"table":{"show":true,"title":true,"ccf":true,"core":true,"unranked":true,"total":true,"other":true,"hidden":true,"note":true},"copy":{"show":true,"summary":true,"table":true,"papers":true,"apa":true,"bibtex":true,"markdown":true,"json":true,"csv":true},"marks":{"show":true,"title":true,"award":true,"oral":true,"spotlight":true,"highlight":true,"grouping":"separate"},"metrics":{"show":true,"title":true,"scope":true,"papers":true,"citations":true,"h":true,"i10":true,"of":true},"years":{"show":true,"title":true,"axis":true},"venues":{"show":true,"title":true},"status":{"show":true,"loaded":true,"cutoff":true,"repeats":true,"absent":true,"unranked":true},"names":{"show":true,"hints":true,"add":true}},"hide":{"cited":false,"citedTable":false,"citedChart":false,"coauthors":false,"access":false},"mergeDuplicates":true,"autoLoad":true}`

## Page events

On a profile page the extension marks the document with `data-rr-ready="true"` (on `<html>`) once it is running; a script on the page can then make calls. It reads what the page shows and sets the page's filters; it cannot read or change the settings.

Dispatch `better-scholar:request` on `document` with `detail: { id, method, params }`; the answer is a `better-scholar:response` event with `detail: { id, ok: true, result }` or `{ id, ok: false, error }`. `id` is a string or a number you choose; it comes back unchanged, so match answers to requests by it.
```js
const id = crypto.randomUUID();
const answer = new Promise((resolve) => {
  const on = (e) => { if (e.detail.id === id) { document.removeEventListener("better-scholar:response", on); resolve(e.detail); } };
  document.addEventListener("better-scholar:response", on);
});
document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("better-scholar:request", { detail: { id, method: "export", params: { format: "bibtex" } } }));
const { result } = await answer;   // result.text is the BibTeX
```

Calls:

### `ping`
Is the extension here, and what is it looking at?
Parameters: none.
Result: { version, owner, loaded, complete } — the extension's version, the profile's name, how many papers are loaded, and whether that is the whole list.

### `summary`
The numbers the panel shows: the role × rank tables, the awards and talks counts, the citation metrics.
Parameters: none.
Result: { owner, loaded, shown, loadingAll, layoutBroken, edition, noRanks, summaries: { ccf, core, none }, marks, metrics: { highlighted, all } } — `summaries.<list>` is { columns, rows: [{ role, A, B, …, total }], totals, hidden, absent, papers }; `marks` counts the papers by award or talk group (the groups the panel counts); `metrics.<which>` is { papers, citations, h, i10 }.

### `papers`
The papers, one record each: who you are in the author list, the venue's ranks, award and talk marks.
Parameters:
  - `filtered`: true (the default): only the papers the page shows now, after the filters; false: every loaded paper.
Result: { owner, total, papers: [{ id, title, authors, venue, year, citations, role, status, highlighted, rank: { ccf: { tier, name } | null, core: { rank, name } | null }, marks: [string], url }] } — `role` is first | cofirst | second | last | middle | null.

### `export`
The papers or the summary as text, in the format of a copy button.
Parameters:
  - `format` (required): summary: the summary as text · table: the summary table, tab-separated · papers: the papers, tab-separated · apa · bibtex · markdown · json (the `papers` records) · csv (RFC 4180).
  - `source`: Which ranking summary and table use (default: the one the panel shows; none: by role only). The other formats ignore it.
Result: { format, text }

### `filter`
Narrow the list the page shows (the filters of the panel). Only the filters named are changed; null clears a number.
Parameters:
  - `query`: The search box's text (syntax below); "" clears it.
  - `onlyHighlighted`: Only the papers where you hold a highlighted position.
  - `yearStart`: Papers from this year on.
  - `yearEnd`: Papers up to this year.
  - `minCitations`: Papers cited at least this often.
  - `impact`: The highlighted papers behind the h-index (at least h citations, h counted over the highlighted papers the other filters let through) or the i10-index (at least 10 citations).
Result: { shown, total, filters: { query, onlyHighlighted, yearStart, yearEnd, minCitations, impact }, errors } — `errors` names the terms of the query that could not be read (an operator with a value it does not take matches nothing).

### `clearFilters`
Remove every filter: the search, a table cell, an awards row, a venue, the year range.
Parameters: none.
Result: { shown, total, filters, errors } — as `filter` returns it, after the filters are cleared.

## Search syntax

The search box and `filter { query }` take words and operators separated by spaces; a paper must match all of them. A word matches the title, authors, venue, the venue's name in the lists, the year, the role and the marks (case does not matter).

- `cites:>100` — citations compared with a number: > >= < <= = (a bare number means =).
- `year:>=2020` — the publication year compared the same way.
- `ccf:a` — the venue's CCF rank: a, b or c.
- `core:a*` — the venue's CORE rank: a*, a, b or c.
- `role:first` — your position in the author list: first, cofirst, second, last, or middle (none of those four).
- `has:award` — has:award — a best-paper award or finalist mark; has:talk — an Oral, Spotlight or Highlight mark.

## Rules for working on this repository

- Chrome first (Manifest V3). No build step and no runtime dependency: `src/` is loaded unpacked.
- `src/lib/` is pure: no DOM and no `chrome.*`. It is unit-tested in Node (`npm test`).
- Precision over recall in venue matching: a missing badge is fine, a wrong one is not.
- Privacy: no network request of the extension's own, except the user-triggered reads of Scholar pages and the opt-in Semantic Scholar title lookup. No analytics, no remote code.
- Every user-visible string is in all 30 `src/_locales/*/messages.json` files (tested). A setting is a row of `SETTINGS` in `src/lib/prefs.js`.
- Everything the extension adds to a Scholar page is prefixed `rr-`.
- Do not name competitors or other extensions in code, tests, commits or documentation.
- Commands: `npm test`, `npm run test:e2e` (Chromium against the stand-in Scholar server), `npm run data`, `npm run agents:doc` (regenerates this file).
